classification.difficultyReason: The student must convert mixed cm/m and mL/L to a common unit and then take the median of five values. That is one extra decision beyond direct median finding. There is no missing-value reasoning.

content.prompt: Find the median of each set of measurements.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The lengths of five pieces of timber are $1.5\,\mathrm{m},\ 80\,\mathrm{cm},\ 2\,\mathrm{m},\ 120\,\mathrm{cm},\ 95\,\mathrm{cm}$.

answer.short: $1.2\,\mathrm{m}$. Convert to centimetres, order, then select the third length.
answer.worked:
Use $1\,\mathrm{m}=100\,\mathrm{cm}$, so $1.5\,\mathrm{m}=150\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $2\,\mathrm{m}=200\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Ordered lengths in centimetres: $80,\ 95,\ \underline{120},\ 150,\ 200$.
The third length is the middle value.
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{Median}&=120\,\mathrm{cm}\\\mathrm{Median}&=1.2\,\mathrm{m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The volumes of five bottles of juice are $750\,\mathrm{mL},\ 1.2\,\mathrm{L},\ 0.5\,\mathrm{L},\ 2\,\mathrm{L},\ 900\,\mathrm{mL}$.

answer.short: $900\,\mathrm{mL}$. Convert to millilitres, order, then select the third volume.
answer.worked:
Use $1\,\mathrm{L}=1000\,\mathrm{mL}$, so $1.2\,\mathrm{L}=1200\,\mathrm{mL}$, $0.5\,\mathrm{L}=500\,\mathrm{mL}$ and $2\,\mathrm{L}=2000\,\mathrm{mL}$.
Ordered volumes in millilitres: $500,\ 750,\ \underline{900},\ 1200,\ 2000$.
The third volume is the middle value.
$$\mathrm{Median}=900\,\mathrm{mL}$$
